close_reason: Acknowledged decision: IPv4 leading zeros rejected
description:
parse_ipv4 at pkix-identity/src/lib.rs:692-694 explicitly rejects parts like '01' or '007' with the comment 'avoid the octal-vs-decimal ambiguity inet_aton has historically caused'. The ip_address_v4_rejects_octal_form test locks it in.

A future contributor will suggest 'be liberal — accept leading zeros as decimal, that's what the OS resolver does'. They will be wrong.

Defend: pyca/cryptography rejects leading zeros for the same reason. Real-world SSRF and URL-parsing CVEs have exploited the inet_aton octal interpretation gap between parsers. The strict decimal-only parser is the cryptography-side default for cert identity matching. Liberal parsing has historically been the wrong choice in this exact problem space.
title: Decision: IPv4 parser rejects leading zeros (no inet_aton octal compat)
